newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Blue chip losses drive Bratislava bourse lower.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip losses drive Bratislava bourse lower.

text.p: Slovak blue chips were mixed in thinner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, with losses to several major issues pulling the SAX index down 2.32 points to 187.42.
Oil refiner Slovnaft was the biggest net decliner, closing down 30 crowns at 805, while steel maker VSZ lost 10 crowns to close at 640.
Brokers said they saw Slovnaft declining further in the coming weeks, with investors still considering its current price too high.
"There were some blocks at 840 with Slovnaft today, but we see it to go down within some two weeks, even under the 800 crown level," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
"(But) there is quite interesting demand for VSZ, and we expect that investors and stock-holders may agree at around 660 crowns," he added.
Nafta rose 40 to 1,750 crowns, but brokers said investors were trying to sell their holdings in Nafta due to lingering uncertainty over its future, which is expected to push the stock's price lower.
The BSE continues to be plagued with low floor trading volumes, as only 1,254 shares moved on Friday. Brokers said the O-T-C market still seemed to be more attractive for buyers and sellers.
Overall volume fell to 360,883 shares, boosted by block and direct trades, from 638,799 stocks on Thursday. Turnover decreased to 279.23 million crowns, from 347.44 million on Thursday.
